title: Alone in the Dark
notes: sound: Game's own Configuration menu (TATOU.COM /INSTALL, F2) run in DOSBox at 20000 cycles: Music = Sound Blaster (OPL FM), Sound effects = Sound Blaster (DMA), keyboard QWERTY. It wrote CONFIG.TAT byte-identical to the shipped one, i.e. the tree was already configured SB/SB-DMA. The drivers detect the card themselves (no IRQ field in the menu).; CRACK.EXE is the [FLT] loader for TATOU.COM; it opens the Infogrames menu - press F1 for Game (proof.png = the attract intro that follows). Real-mode, ran with ems=false/umb=false. At cycles=max the configuration menu's card detection found NOTHING (music 'No possible choice', SFX stuck on Buzzer); it only detected the SB at 20000 cycles - it is a speed-sensitive probe. Harmless here because CONFIG.TAT already holds SB, but if anyone re-runs Configuration on the P166 and it lists no cards, that is the cause. Sound output with IRQ 5 not verified by ear.

The shipped CONFIG.BS6 selects Sound Effects AdLib/Sound Blaster, Digitized Sound Blaster, Music AdLib/Sound Blaster (OPL FM) - confirmed in the in-game Sound Settings screen in DOSBox; nothing changed (the game rewrites its last config byte on quit).; v2.00R. The registered exe checks FILE_ID.DIZ and, without it, prints 'Critical file FILE_ID.DIZ missing or modified' on the way out (seen in DOSBox). FILE_ID.DIZ is Apogee's registered-copy notice text, written by running once the TRSi CRACK.EXE shipped in the DGC Rev2 zip (it writes the file, then starts the game); CRACK.EXE itself is not staged. With it, the game quits cleanly to Apogee's commercial-version exit screen. The v2.10G update (DGC Rev2.1, scl-agup.zip, installs over Rev2) was tried and rejected: its BS_AOG.EXE refuses to start with 'FILE_ID.DIZ missing or modified' and no matching FILE_ID.DIZ exists on the share; Rev2 alone also lacks SVSWAP.BS6. Proven in DOSBox 0.74 with ems=false/umb=false: intro, menus, mission 1 gameplay, clean quit. Not tested in a real Win98 DOS box.

notes: sound: Game's own SETUP.EXE (HMI SOS) run in DOSBox at 30000 cycles: its System Info detected 'SB16 ST port 220 DMA 1 IRQ 5'; Sound card set explicitly to SB16 ST, port 220, DMA 1, IRQ 5 (its Auto Detect picks SB16 MONO - not used) and saved (Y). The cracked STARTH.EXE (identical in DOSFILL and DGC) dies in DOSBox 0.74 right after its 'cracked by Hoson of Hybrid' banner with 'Error [35]: Unexpected Interrupt=0027 in DOS4GW.EXE at 0160:061E' - every variation tried fails (cycles max/30000/10000, core normal, cputype 486/pentium/auto, ems on (->0029), xms off (->0026), no SB, no joystick, 16 MB, loadfix, a CD drive mounted); cracked STARTL.EXE takes DOSBox itself down ('IRET: Illegal descriptor'). title: Spear of Destiny - Mission Packs
notes: sound: Same engine as Spear of Destiny - no setup program, BLASTER (A220 I5 D1) is read by SPEAR.EXE. SOD.EXE keeps one CONFIG.SDn per mission and swaps it to CONFIG.SOD; each CONFIG.SD1/SD2/SD3 is a copy of the game's own shipped CONFIG.SOD (Sound Effects AdLib/SB, Digitized SB, Music AdLib/SB FM). Mission 3 was seen starting with that config (full-size view).; SOD.EXE is FormGen's mission menu (1 original, 2 Return to Danger, 3 Ultimate Challenge, 4 Mission Generator, 0 exit): it RENAMES the chosen mission's GAMEMAPS/VSWAP (and copies MAPHEAD, swaps CONFIG) from .SDn to .SOD, renames the previous set back, then runs SPEAR.EXE. GAMEGEN.EXE (what DOSFILL named as launcher) is the level editor, not the game. The staged tree is the pristine state: the original mission's GAMEMAPS/MAPHEAD/VSWAP renamed .SD1 and no active .SOD map set - with the originals left as .SOD, SOD.EXE mistook them for mission 4 and overwrote the original MAPHEAD. Proven in DOSBox (ems=false): menu, mission 2 and mission 3 gameplay, and a switch back to mission 1 that restored the original files byte-identical. SPEAR.EXE run directly from the pristine tree finds no maps - always launch SOD.EXE. Unproven: the tree MUTATES at every mission switch, and GAMESYNC never deletes - a later re-sync onto a box that has switched missions would re-add the .SDn files beside the renamed .SOD set; purge the title before any resync. Not tested in a real Win98 DOS box.
